data.narrative:
Terrestrial Energy is a public-stage nuclear energy company that has raised $280M to date. The nuclear energy sector comprises a fragmented peer universe of 10 comparable companies across public and private markets: three public peers (OKLO, NNE, SMR) and seven private-stage companies including Oklo, Helion, Valar Atomics, X-Energy, and Nano Nuclear Energy.

The peer-median method is not applicable to this valuation. A systematic screen for same-stage, adjacent-stage, and similar-valuation-tier peers yielded insufficient datapoints—only one company met narrow stage and tier criteria, falling short of the three-company minimum threshold required for robust median analysis. While six same-sector peers exist in nuclear energy, their heterogeneity across stage, technology maturity, and capital structure precludes meaningful cross-sectional median benchmarking.

Without sufficient narrow-peer triangulation, this analysis cannot support a quantitative valuation range. The market remains early-stage and fragmented; deriving multiples from all-sector medians would mask material differences in technology readiness, regulatory pathway, and unit economics among nuclear subsegments. Further development of the private-peer dataset—particularly post-valuation rounds from Helion, X-Energy, or Valar Atomics—would enable credible comparable-company analysis. Until then, valuation should rely on discounted cash flow modeling anchored to technology milestones and deployment timelines rather than trading multiples.
